classification.difficultyReason: Interprets a ditch below the launch origin and solves a quadratic using the specified gravitational acceleration.

content.prompt: A ball is thrown at $45^\circ$ at $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and lands in a $10\text{ m}$ deep ditch. Using $g=9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find, to 1 d.p.:

spec.description: Launch-origin axes, rising and falling parabolic trajectory, launch vector and angle, ditch floor below the launch level, and a vertical depth dimension. The vertical coordinate is exaggerated for the schematic view; no numeric axis scale is asserted.
spec.mathematics: Physical trajectory y=x-(9.8/900)x^2; launch angle 45 degrees, speed 30 m/s, landing level y=-10. Drawing coordinates use five times the physical vertical displacement.
spec.answerVisibility: All labels and geometry are permanent question givens; no calculated flight time or range is shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: how long it takes to land,

answer.worked:
Take the launch point as the origin, with upwards positive. The ditch floor is at $y=-10$.
$$\begin{align*}
\dot{x}&=30\cos45^\circ=15\sqrt2\\
\dot{y}&=-9.8t+30\sin45^\circ=-9.8t+15\sqrt2\\
y&=-4.9t^2+15\sqrt2\,t\\
-10&=-4.9t^2+15\sqrt2\,t\\
4.9t^2-15\sqrt2\,t-10&=0\\
t&=\frac{15\sqrt2+\sqrt{450+196}}{9.8}\\
t&\approx4.8\text{ s}.
\end{align*}$$
The negative root is rejected because $t>0$.

Using the unrounded flight time,
$$\begin{align*}
x&=15\sqrt2\left(\frac{15\sqrt2+\sqrt{646}}{9.8}\right)\\
x&\approx100.9\text{ m}.
\end{align*}$$
